generatedFrom: a REAL ceremony on an acceptance environment, 2026-08-13
note: Unlike the v2 and v4 vectors this is NOT a throwaway key but a genuine signature, set by a remote signing service with a certificate from a test issuing CA. Deliberate: v5 went into use with no vector covering it, and the first full end-to-end walk found the verifier checking the wrong source. A self-invented case would mostly have proven that one author's writer and reader agree.
rules: The seal image belongs INSIDE the signing input: it is embedded during the ceremony and falls under what is signed (§a.8).
What must be checked is reconstruction: the signing input derived from the document alone equals the recorded one, and its sha256 equals the digest the service signed.
Trust in the chain is the verifier's question (§c.4), not this vector's.

cases.name: real-ceremony-with-seal
cases.note: Markdown with an embedded seal image. This is the case a v5 implementation is most likely to get wrong: the appearance is part of the signed content, not decoration around it.
